Things you need to know before buying a property in Dubai! And here’s a Detailed cost breakdown of a residential property – For Mortgage properties

Follow @geethika.kirpa for more details on your first property in Dubai! 😍

You can let me know if you have any questions in the comment section! 🙂

1. Down-payment 20% (max. Loan-to-Value 80%)
Banks typically lend 80% of the property valuation (done by a 3rd-party), not the negotiated final price—so if valuation is below the negotiated price, you’ll need extra cash, which luckily didn’t happen in our case.

2. DLD Land Department Fee 4% of property value — mandatory transfer fee plus some extra admin charges AED 580

3. Brokerage Commission 2% + 5% VAT (on that commission)

4. Other Fees ~1–2% of property price, including:
a. Trustee fee: AED 4,000 + AED 200 VAT = AED 4,200
b. Valuation fee: ~AED 2,000–3,500 depending on bank (can vary further)
c. Trustee-office/mortgage-transfer admin fees: ~AED 3,000 total
d. Building NOC fee: AED 500–2,000 (depending on developer – can vary further)
e. Manager’s cheque: AED 75–105 for each cheque
f. Mortgage processing: 0.5% of loan amount – This is actually kinda informally negotiable; we negotiated with our financial agent and managed to waive this off

✨ Total upfront cash needed: ~27–30% of property price. Add a buffer for renovations/contingencies → better to budget 35–40% in bank

That’s exactly why escrow accounts exist in Dubai. 🏗️🔐

For off-plan projects, your payments go into a regulated project escrow account — the developer doesn’t simply receive the entire amount upfront.

Funds are released progressively as the project reaches construction milestones. So the developer doesn’t have access to your entire investment from Day 1.

That’s one of the important safeguards when buying off-plan property in Dubai. 🇦🇪
